images.title: Taking away negative tokens
images.purpose: Show that after putting in 6 zero pairs to +4, taking away the 6 negative tokens leaves 10 positive tokens.
images.composition: One long row of tokens centred, one outlined group beneath it, equation centred below with wide space.
images.exact_structure: One row of exactly 10 teal #0072B2 positive tokens, evenly spaced. Directly beneath the right-hand 6 of them, exactly 6 amber #E69F00 negative tokens, one under each, all enclosed together in one reddish purple #CC79A7 rounded outline. Under the left-hand 4 teal tokens there is nothing. Exactly 10 teal tokens, 6 amber tokens, 1 outline.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
amber tokens under fewer or more than 6 teal tokens
images.takeaway: Taking away negative tokens leaves more positive tokens, so the value goes up.
images.description: A row of 10 teal positive tokens with 6 amber negative tokens outlined under the last 6; taking those 6 away leaves 10 positive, so +4 − (−6) = +10.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the teal tokens that stay, then say whether the value went up or down.

image_decisions.why: Taking away negative tokens supplied by zero pairs is a picture idea; one clean image carries it.
